editorial:
Ever felt like you were taking your partner for granted until someone else showed interest? That is exactly where you find yourself with Victor and Suzanne. He is a free-spirited painter who loves his art and his girlfriend, but he just cannot wrap his head around why she wants a formal commitment. Suzanne is tired of the guessing games and wants to know where she stands. It is a classic battle of wills set in a charming 1960s world, and the vibe is light, breezy, and full of playful tension. You will find yourself laughing at Victor's cluelessness while rooting for Suzanne to finally get the answer she deserves.

What really makes this movie work is the great chemistry between the leads and the funny way the plot twists when a new suitor enters the mix. The pacing is snappy, and it does not feel dated despite its age. While some might find the plot a bit simple, it is the perfect kind of movie to relax with on a Friday night. You should definitely look for this one to stream in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best colors, or you can rent it on Apple TV if you are short on time. If you love owning a physical copy, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your collection is a great move.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when Victor realizes he cannot stand the thought of losing Suzanne to another man. After spending the movie avoiding commitment, he finally has a wake-up call. He stops playing games and openly admits his love and need for her. The movie wraps up with Victor finally giving Suzanne the reassurance and formal commitment she wanted all along, proving that he learned his lesson the hard way.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old-school romantic comedies and stories about love and jealousy.
